doc.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Growing up and learning drums in Washington
title: Five years of development and lessons with Jack Denay
summary: Cobb dates his development from 1945 to 1950, says he had about five lessons with Denay, and recalls Denay's late phone call.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: From the time that you became interested in drums to the time you started to play professionally, to gig, what were – how much – three years? four years?
I would say maybe five years. I would say from ’45 to ’50. I left at ’50.
How many lessons did you have with the classical guy?
Not many. I don’t remember having too many.

No, not that many. Maybe five. Not ten or nothing like that, because one way or another we got separated. The band left town or something like that. Something changed where I couldn’t – we couldn’t get together.
What did he give you? What did he show you?

He gave me some technique about the snare drum. That’s what I wanted from him, to learn about the snare drum. Had I stayed there long enough, I probably would have learned the whole percussion thing from him, because he was going to teach me free. It would have been a matter of time of just doing it with him. But we got separated some time. I don’t even remember how. I remember, way later in my lifetime, I got a call one day. He called up. He said, “This is Jack Denay. I read somewhere where you mention my name every once in a while.” I say, “Yeah, man, how you doing?” By that time, he was 70, 80 years old or something like that. He said, “I’m doing okay.” I said, “I’m sure glad to talk with you. I always give you the benefit of being one of my leaders. I just wanted you to know that.” He found out how – a way to get in touch with me.
